title: Prove exact Coxeter tariffs with arbitrary dirty workspace
body:
The existing symmetric-group and dihedral cut arguments settle particular noncommuting alphabets, leaving other reflection systems and arbitrarily large dirty workspaces open. This contribution proves one uniform exact tariff for **every finite-rank Coxeter system**, including infinite groups, arbitrary heterogeneous diagonal targets, and any finite number of restored dirty registers.

Each root orbit gives its own sharp paid-call lower bound. Reduced words attain all orbit bounds simultaneously, so the result permits every positive price constant on reflection conjugacy classes. For the new concrete family B_n, the exact tariff is `a*neg(w) + b*(inv(w)+nsp(w))` per target, for every n and every positive sign-flip/swap price pair. An explicitly rank-priced extension allows arbitrary binary scalar couplings, including nilpotents.

This is a uniform **mechanism exclusion**, not a new supplier or improved kappa. It rules out sharing savings throughout the stated simple-reflection model. Non-class-invariant prices, arbitrary involution-generated groups such as the GL3 coordinate-CNOT alphabet, additional quotient relations, native realization and nonlinear recursive pricing remain outside the theorem.

Only `research/coxeter-root-tariff/` is added. Read `README.md` for the result and coverage, `PROOF.md` for the all-parameter argument, and `REVIEW.md` for the separate AI proof/code review with exact hashes. `SOURCES.json`, `EXTERNAL-SOURCES.json`, `OVERLAP.json`, and `TASK.json` retain sources, scope, selection and freshness. The scientific baseline is 7f90cb99; the submission branch was rebased onto refreshed canonical main 0374b3e6, whose relevant guidance and scientific inputs are unchanged.

Validation:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/coxeter-root-tariff
```

The full registered replay passes locally on Python 3.12.15. It includes:

- All 1,946 elements of nine finite Coxeter systems through F4, an exact affine-A2 radius-nine probe, all 530 binary couplings through three roles, and 64 full-formal B2 target pairs.
- A separately implemented signed-window/Dijkstra checker: all 4,282 B1–B5 elements and 12,846 exact weighted tariff comparisons, plus heterogeneous formal circuits with one to three genuinely coupled dirty helpers.
- Six integrity test groups, including read-only Git-free exports, missing/corrupted source pins, typed/duplicate-key receipts, and an actual rank-undercharging mutation. Normal/optimized replays also pass on Python 3.14.7; direct checks pass on 3.11.3.

The proof explicitly handles infinite direct sums with finite crossing ranks. The tests distinguish formal endpoints from their nonfaithful root-module images. Finite checks corroborate the written theorem; they do not establish the infinite conclusion by enumeration. No selected cold replay, Lean/kernel proof, native implementation or human review is claimed.

Credit Adam Gall, Ross Richardson, the retained finite-dihedral contributors and register-model lineage, Gert Heckman's standard Coxeter root theory, and ywz65/PR2716's earlier infinite-dihedral rank-priced extension. All previously settled symmetric/dihedral cases, including D16 workspace, are inherited rather than claimed as new. Prepared for David Arias with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate AI review and an independent implementation. Apache-2.0. No selected frontier or frozen input is changed.
